code: # spigot "live" example: a counter shared by every open tab. It uses all three # channels between a page and R: # # * HTTP: the page reads and changes the count with spigot.get() and #   spigot.post() (api.R). # * Push: R sends every open tab the new count with spigot_broadcast(), and #   the page listens with spigot.on(). # * Bridge: the endpoint also sets an input of the calling tab with #   spigot_trigger(), so that tab's server function updates a Shiny output #   on the page. # # Run it with spigot::run_example("live"), then open the page in a second tab. library(shiny) library(spigot)  # State shared by every tab. It lives in this R process, so the endpoints in # api.R (evaluated in this environment) and the server function see the same # values. shared <- new.env() shared$count <- 0L shared$tabs <- 0L  server <- function(input, output, session) {   # A tab opened or closed: tell every tab how many are open.   shared$tabs <- shared$tabs + 1L   spigot_broadcast("tabs", list(tabs = shared$tabs))   session$onSessionEnded(function() {     shared$tabs <- shared$tabs - 1L     spigot_broadcast("tabs", list(tabs = shared$tabs))   })    # This tab's own clicks. The increment endpoint sets input$clicked with   # spigot_trigger(); the page shows output$mine in an element with the   # class "shiny-text-output".   mine <- reactiveVal(0L)   observeEvent(input$clicked, mine(mine() + input$clicked))   output$mine <- renderText(mine()) }  spigot_app(   pages = spigot_page("index.html"),   server = server,   api = "api.R" ) # The example's API. `shared` is defined in app.R: spigot_app() evaluates this # file in app.R's environment.  #* The count and the number of open tabs. A plain HTTP read. #* @get /state function() {   list(count = shared$count, tabs = shared$tabs) }  #* Add `by` (1 to 10) to the count, tell every tab, and tell this tab's #* server function. #* @post /increment function(req, res, by = 1) {   by <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(by))   if (length(by) != 1 || is.na(by) || by < 1 || by > 10) {     res$status <- 400L     return(list(error = "by must be a whole number from 1 to 10"))   }   shared$count <- shared$count + by    # Push: every open tab, this one included, gets the new count.   spigot_broadcast("count", list(count = shared$count, by = by))   # Bridge: this tab's server function sees input$clicked change.   spigot_trigger(spigot_session(req), "clicked", by)    list(count = shared$count) } // The page's only script. spigot_app() adds spigot.js, which defines spigot.get(), // spigot.post() and spigot.on().  const $ = (id) => document.getElementById(id);  // The count only goes up, so show the highest value seen. A reply and a push // can arrive in either order: R sends the push while the endpoint runs, so it // can reach the page before the reply to the same request. let shown = -1; function showCount(n) {   if (n <= shown) return;   shown = n;   $("count").textContent = n; }  const lines = []; function log(line) {   lines.push(`${new Date().toLocaleTimeString()}  ${line}`);   $("log").textContent = lines.slice(-10).join("\n"); }  // Push: R calls spigot_broadcast() when the count changes or a tab opens or closes. spigot.on("count", (msg) => {   showCount(msg.count);   log(`push  count: ${msg.count} (+${msg.by})`); }); spigot.on("tabs", (msg) => {   $("tabs").textContent = msg.tabs;   log(`push  tabs: ${msg.tabs}`); });  // HTTP: read the current state once. spigot.get() waits for the Shiny session. spigot.get("state").then((s) => {   showCount(s.count);   $("tabs").textContent = s.tabs; });  async function add(by) {   try {     const reply = await spigot.post("increment", { by });     showCount(reply.count);     log(`reply count: ${reply.count}`);   } catch (err) {     if (!(err instanceof spigot.SpigotError)) throw err;     log(`reply ${err.status}: ${err.message}`);   } }  $("plus-one").addEventListener("click", () => add(1)); $("plus-five").addEventListener("click", () => add(5)); $("plus-bad").addEventListener("click", () => add(11));
